javascript-fundamentals-sr3-03.reason: ambiguous: in strict code a function declaration inside a nested block is hoisted only to the top of that block, so 'a function declaration' in general could be defended as False. You can use the function before you declared it' and 'In strict mode, block-level function declarations are scoped to that block and are hoisted to the top of the block.' (final: fixed)
javascript-fundamentals-sr3-03.statement: A function declaration at the top level of a function body is callable from lines above it.
javascript-fundamentals-sr3-03.explanation: A function declaration directly in a function body is hoisted to the top of that function, so earlier lines can call it. In strict mode, one inside a nested block is hoisted only to the top of that block.

javascript-fundamentals-sr4-12.reason: ambiguous: the answer flips with the mode of f, so the mode now sits inside the statement. MDN call(), thisArg: 'If the function is not in strict mode, null and undefined will be replaced with the global object, and primitive values will be converted to objects.' (final: keep)
javascript-fundamentals-sr4-12.statement: In strict mode, `function f(){return this;}` called as `f.call(7)` returns the primitive Number `7`.
javascript-fundamentals-sr4-12.explanation: In strict mode, call passes its thisArg to f unchanged, so this is the primitive 7. A non-strict function would receive a Number wrapper object instead.

javascript-fundamentals-sr9-10.reason: ambiguous: 'schedules a promise reaction' also covers a then() on a pending promise, where the timer can run first. The rewrite uses an already fulfilled promise and also drops the 'when' and 'browser' tells. MDN Microtask_guide: 'Promises use the microtask queue for their callbacks', setTimeout() callbacks are tasks, and microtasks run 'before the next task is run'. The page's example logs main, microtask, timeout. (final: keep)
javascript-fundamentals-sr9-10.statement: If a task runs `setTimeout(b, 0); Promise.resolve().then(a);`, `b` runs before `a`.
javascript-fundamentals-sr9-10.explanation: Promise.resolve() is already fulfilled, so a is queued as a microtask and runs once the task's code ends. b is a timer callback, which runs in a later task, so a runs first.
javascript-fundamentals-sr9-10.misconception: A zero-delay timer scheduled first runs before a promise reaction queued later in the same task.

javascript-fundamentals-sr10-12.reason: tell: an 'In ES2026,' opener marked False (2T/6F in the deck, every b3 instance false). Switched to the 'Since ES2026,' frame. Fact and answer unchanged. (final: keep)
javascript-fundamentals-sr10-12.statement: Since ES2026, `Error.isError()` returns false for an Error created in another realm.
javascript-fundamentals-sr10-12.explanation: Error.isError recognizes genuine Error objects across realms and returns true for them. It uses an internal brand rather than the current realm's Error.prototype chain.
javascript-fundamentals-sr10-12.misconception: Error.isError shares instanceof Error's rejection of errors from another realm.

javascript-fundamentals-sr9-08.reason: tell: an 'In ES2026,' opener marked False. Switched to the 'Since ES2026,' frame. Fact and answer unchanged. (final: fixed)
javascript-fundamentals-sr9-08.statement: Since ES2026, `Array.fromAsync()` takes the next value from a sync iterable before the previous promise settles.
javascript-fundamentals-sr9-08.explanation: Array.fromAsync iterates lazily: it awaits each promise a sync iterable yields and takes the next value only after that one settles, unlike Promise.all, which reads every value first.
javascript-fundamentals-sr9-08.misconception: Array.fromAsync eagerly retrieves every input before it starts awaiting input values.

javascript-fundamentals-sr4-10.reason: tell: a conditional 'when' clause marked False (3T/10F). Removed 'when called' and shortened the statement. Fact and answer unchanged. (final: keep)
javascript-fundamentals-sr4-10.statement: An arrow defined inside a regular function gets its own `arguments` object.
javascript-fundamentals-sr4-10.explanation: The arrow uses the enclosing regular function's arguments binding. Passing different arguments to the arrow does not replace that enclosing arguments object.
javascript-fundamentals-sr4-10.misconception: An arrow creates an arguments object for its own call.

javascript-fundamentals-sr12-12.reason: tell: a 'When' conditional opener marked False. Reframed with 'With', which a true r12 card also uses. Fact and answer unchanged. (final: keep)
javascript-fundamentals-sr12-12.statement: With a truthy `x`, the expression `x ||= compute()` evaluates the `compute()` call.
javascript-fundamentals-sr12-12.explanation: For a truthy x, ||= skips its right-hand side and makes no assignment. The compute() call is therefore skipped.
javascript-fundamentals-sr12-12.misconception: Logical OR assignment evaluates its right-hand side even when the existing value is truthy.

javascript-fundamentals-sr8-06.reason: tell: a 'When' conditional opener marked False. Reworded without the conditional. Fact and answer unchanged. (final: keep)
javascript-fundamentals-sr8-06.statement: Rejection of the `Promise.all()` result cancels the other operations represented by its inputs.
javascript-fundamentals-sr8-06.explanation: Promise.all rejection does not cancel its input operations. Pending operations can continue independently of the rejected aggregate promise.
javascript-fundamentals-sr8-06.misconception: Promise.all cancels remaining input operations when it rejects.

javascript-fundamentals-sr5-01.statement: An own property whose value is `undefined` shadows a same-named property on the prototype.
javascript-fundamentals-sr5-01.explanation: Property lookup stops at an own property even when its value is undefined. JavaScript does not continue up the prototype chain looking for a different value.

javascript-fundamentals-sr6-04.statement: A module reruns its top-level initialization for another importer of the same resolved module.
javascript-fundamentals-sr6-04.explanation: Importers of the same resolved module share its evaluation. Another import reuses that module instead of rerunning its top-level initialization.
javascript-fundamentals-sr6-04.misconception: A module repeats its initialization for each importer.

javascript-fundamentals-sr10-11.statement: For `new AggregateError(new Set(['a', 'b']))`, `errors` is an array containing 'a' and 'b'.
